answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a slashable bond held in escrow, like a harbor charging each ship a deposit before it may dock. New identities start with near-zero trust and earn standing only through verified work, so a Sybil farmer who plants an orchard of fake agents must fund a bond for each one. Periodic uniqueness re-checks act like water seeping through karst: cheap identities dissolve under scrutiny, and any duplicate proof slashes the whole bond, making mass fakery cost far more than it can ever earn.
